title: Nvidia Studio Space
tagline: A multi-city event platform for NVIDIA Studio, built to handle registration, content delivery, and real-time attendee engagement across Cairo and Dubai.
overview:
Nvidia Studio Space is a flagship NVIDIA-branded event platform delivered across multiple cities, designed to host creators, artists, and content producers. The platform handles ticketed registration, scheduled content, speaker profiles, live scanning of attendees, and localized English/Arabic experiences.

Built on a modular Laravel architecture with Livewire Volt components, it integrates with Paymob for payments and Zoho Inventory for merchandise fulfillment, all while maintaining performance at peak event load.
challenge: NVIDIA needed a single platform that could serve multiple event hubs (Cairo, Dubai, and beyond) with distinct branding, schedules, and languages — while feeding into a unified analytics and check-in system. Legacy solutions couldn't handle the bilingual RTL/LTR experience, offline scanning at the venue, or the tight Zoho/Paymob integration requirements.
solution:
I architected a multi-schema PostgreSQL backend with dedicated `events` and `management` schemas, using Laravel's modular structure to isolate each hub's content while sharing core services. The operator scanning interface uses the native BarcodeDetector API with a jsQR fallback, and IndexedDB queues scans offline for sync when connectivity returns.

Paymob integration supports multi-ticket types and discount codes with a webhook proxy for reliable delivery, and a dedicated `CriticalErrorHandler` service sends HTML email alerts the moment anything in the payment or inventory pipeline fails.

features.description: A single codebase serves Cairo, Dubai, and future hubs with isolated content, speakers, and scheduling.

features.description: Multi-ticket checkout with discount codes, webhook proxy, and Zoho contact sync.

features.description: Full Arabic and English support with directional-aware layouts across the entire platform.

features.title: Real-time analytics
features.description: Organizers see attendee flow, scan rates, and ticket sales live on a Livewire dashboard.

results: The platform launched successfully in Cairo and Dubai with zero payment-pipeline failures. The offline-first scanning kept check-in flowing even during peak venue load, and the modular architecture meant rolling out the Dubai hub took days instead of weeks.

overview: Nvidia Office is NVIDIA's dedicated content and engagement destination within the ArabHardware network. It aggregates driver news, technical deep-dives, hardware reviews, and community content with full Arabic localization.

title: ArabHardware Platform
tagline: The flagship Arabic-language tech content network — delivering reviews, news, events, and community across the MENA region to millions of readers.
overview:
ArabHardware is the MENA region's leading Arabic tech publication, covering hardware, gaming, AI, and emerging technology. The platform hosts 55,000+ articles, a high-traffic events module, a growing store, and community features — all built on a unified Laravel foundation.

I'm responsible for the backend architecture, performance optimization, and most of the major feature modules including Events, Editors/CMS, Store, HR, Ads, and Users.
challenge: The legacy platform couldn't scale with the growing content volume or the business ambitions — events, e-commerce, HR, and multiple brand sub-sites. A full migration from Laravel 9 to Laravel 12 was needed without dropping any of the 55,000+ existing posts or breaking SEO.
solution:
I designed a modular Laravel 12 architecture on PostgreSQL with dedicated schemas per domain (`posts`, `media`, `events`, `store`, `hr`, `ads`, `management`). Each module owns its data and exposes a clean interface, which made it trivial to spin up branded sub-experiences (Nvidia, Lenovo, Ubisoft) without code duplication.

The migration preserved all URLs and SEO equity, moved user auth to Spatie roles, and normalized phone numbers and other legacy inconsistencies in the process.

title: ArabHardware Store (AHW Hub)
tagline: A comprehensive Zoho Inventory ↔ Shopify synchronization engine powering ArabHardware's e-commerce operation with zero-downtime duplicate prevention and real-time stock accuracy.
overview: The AHW Hub is a production-grade sync system that keeps Zoho Inventory (source of truth for stock, cost, purchase orders) and Shopify (customer-facing store) in perfect alignment. It handles products, customers, inventory levels, and purchase orders with full audit trails and rate-limit-aware API consumption.
challenge: Previous sync attempts suffered from duplicate products, stock desynchronization, webhook replay issues, and opaque failure modes. Every failure meant manual reconciliation and angry customers. The team needed a system they could trust — with alerts, dashboards, and rollback paths.
solution:
I built the sync on a modular Laravel foundation with dedicated store schema tables for `item_mappings`, `customer_mappings`, and audit logs. Duplicate prevention enforces uniqueness at the SKU+title level; webhook deduplication tracks every payload by ID+event with idempotency windows.

The dashboard reads exclusively from the local enriched tables (no live Shopify/Zoho calls per page view), with a GraphQL-based diff scanner running on a queue to detect drift. A `CriticalErrorHandler` service sends HTML-formatted email alerts within seconds of any pipeline failure.

title: Palestine Crisis Tracker

overview: A personal project built to make the Palestine crisis data more accessible and humane. It pulls from public data sources and presents the information with careful typography and non-sensationalized visuals.
challenge: Data about ongoing conflicts is often scattered, behind paywalls, or presented in dehumanizing ways. The goal was to create a single accessible view that respects the gravity of the subject.
solution: A lightweight static site that fetches and caches public data, with clear sourcing and update timestamps. The interface leans on minimal typography and slow, intentional animations rather than alarming visuals.
